exercises.title: Prioritisation 1 — why and when
exercises.problemHtml:
Prioritisation (requirements triage) reveals competing goals, resolves conflicts, plans staged deliveries, controls scope creep and supports trade-off decisions. Establish priorities early, when you have the most flexibility, and revisit them periodically. Davis’ pragmatics: customers’ needs, relative importance, timing, predecessors, requirements that must be implemented as a group, and cost.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

# Prioritisation 1 — why and when — answer key

1. When should priorities be set?Khi nào đặt ưu tiên?
   Answer: a) Early, and revisited periodically as the project and business change
   Early = most flexibility.VI: Sớm = linh hoạt nhất.

2. FR-8 "Export to PDF" cannot work before FR-3 "Generate report". Which pragmatic issue is this?FR-8 "Xuất PDF" không thể chạy trước FR-3 "Tạo báo cáo". Đây là vấn đề nào?
   Answer: a) Predecessors (dependencies)
   A predecessor must come first.VI: Yêu cầu tiên quyết phải đi trước.

3. Is priority the same as importance?Ưu tiên có giống tầm quan trọng không?
   Answer: a) No — importance is weighed against timing, dependencies and cost
   Priority is a trade-off.VI: Ưu tiên là một sự đánh đổi.

exercises.title: Prioritisation 2 — games and the questions that expose them
exercises.problemHtml:
Avoid decibel prioritisation (the loudest voice wins) and threat prioritisation (whoever holds the most political power wins). Wiegers’ questions to get stakeholders to admit lower priorities: Is there another way to satisfy the need? What are the consequences of omitting or deferring it? What is the effect on the business objectives if it waits several months? Is it worth delaying the release of everything else? Classify each situation or question.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Prioritisation 4 — in or out for release 1
exercises.problemHtml:
The simplest technique: stakeholders go down the list and decide in or out for the first release, constantly referring to the business objectives, paring the list to the bare minimum. Business objective of ClinicCare release 1: "Let patients book and cancel appointments online to cut phone calls to reception by 40% within 6 months."

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Prioritisation 3 — pairwise comparison and rank ordering
exercises.problemHtml:
In pairwise comparison, stakeholders judge, for each pair of features, which is more important; ranking by number of "wins" gives an order. It works for a small set (features, quality attributes) but becomes unwieldy beyond a couple of dozen items (n(n−1)/2 comparisons). Write:

  • function pairs(n) — how many comparisons are needed for n items.
  • function rankPairwise(items, judgements) — judgements is an array of [winner, loser]. Return the item ids sorted by number of wins (most first); ties keep the order of items. Ignore judgements that mention unknown items or compare an item with itself; if the same pair is judged more than once, only the last judgement counts.

Requirements

  • pairs(20) = 190 — why the method does not scale to hundreds of requirements.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
So sánh từng cặp: với mỗi cặp, chọn cái quan trọng hơn; xếp theo số lần thắng. Viết pairs(n) (số phép so sánh) và rankPairwise(items, judgements): sắp theo số thắng giảm dần, hoà giữ thứ tự items; bỏ phán xét có mục lạ hoặc tự so với mình; cùng một cặp phán xét nhiều lần ⇒ chỉ lần cuối tính.

Yêu cầu

  • pairs(20) = 190 — vì sao không dùng được cho hàng trăm yêu cầu.

examplesJson.explanation: C 2 wins, A 1, B 0.|||C thắng 2, A 1, B 0.
